title: Building a robust and diversified clearing ecosystem
summary: Fabio Panetta, ECB Executive Board Member, delivered a speech on March 22, 2022 discussing the resilience of central counterparties (CCPs) amid multiple crises including COVID-19, supply chain disruptions, and the Russian invasion of Ukraine. He emphasized the need for a diversified global clearing ecosystem, noting that the EU has room to expand clearing capacity given the size of its economy and the euro's international role. He also outlined priorities for safely evolving the clearing ecosystem, including addressing climate risk and crypto-asset regulation.
key_points: CCPs have weathered multiple shocks in recent years: COVID-19 crisis, supply chain bottlenecks, energy and commodity price rises, and the Russian invasion of Ukraine fallout
ESMA is reviewing anti-procyclicality requirements for CCPs, examining margin procyclicality and system-wide impact under higher market volatility

Panetta argued that financial markets are more stable when market participants have options for where to clear, and expressed concern about over-dependence on a small number of providers for systemic clearing activities
The European Commission launched a targeted consultation to build EU clearing capacity and revise the supervisory framework for CCPs with significant cross-border services
CCPs are assessing new technologies including distributed ledger technology and cloud computing to enhance efficiency of IT processes
ESMA is developing a climate risk stress test for CCPs, which the ECB is actively supporting
Panetta emphasized that crypto-assets and clearing activities in that space must comply with strictest standards including KYC, AML, and disclosure requirements
why_it_matters: This speech provides insight into ECB thinking on critical market infrastructure resilience. The emphasis on clearing ecosystem diversification and the review of margin procyclicality directly affects how CCPs manage risk and how clearing members respond to market stress. Market participants should note the direction of EU regulatory evolution on CCP supervision and anti-procyclicality rules. Historical record of early ECB response to Ukraine crisis impact on clearing infrastructure.
